topic: Decoder-competition vs feature-fragmentation in F-category specificity failures

design.probe_a: Greedy decoding (do_sample=False, T=0, freq_penalty=0) with the same intervention.
design.probe_b: One-shot logit bias (-8.0) on competitor token IDs at first generated step, then greedy argmax + unsteered continuation.

pairs.probe_b_continuation_at_m_4_47:
The capital of the state containing Fargo is Raleigh.

The state of North Dakota is located in the Midwest region of the
pairs.key_observation: At M=4.47 the steered logits put Raleigh and Chapel both at p=0.121 (exact tie). Greedy decoding picks Chapel by token-id tie-break. After suppressing the NC non-capital cluster, Raleigh becomes the unique top-1 and the model emits the correct capital coherently.

Montpelier prefix ' Mont' is at rank 1320-6576 across all M. Top-5 at M=20 contains [' Interv', ' Shel', ' Lyndon', ' VT', ' Agency'] -- VT-flavoured but no Montpelier. Suppression moves the rank by at most 2.
Juneau rank stays at 13-273 across all M even after suppressing 12 AK-non-capital tokens. Suppression lifts the rank but never into the top-10. Argmax becomes generic noise after suppression.

conclusions.decoder_competition_definition: Target capital is in steered top-2 at some M; failure is purely sampler/tie-break.
conclusions.feature_fragmentation_definition: Target capital is outside steered top-100 at all M; capital signal is missing from intervention.
decoder_competition_recoverable_by: greedy decoding when target is the unique argmax
moving steering off the OOD-collapse regime (M < 12)
feature_fragmentation_likely_requires: different feature selection (target-graph features that actually encode the capital token)
direct token-level injection (e.g. logit bias on the answer token)
alternate prompt that primes the capital concept directly

open_questions: Population fraction: of the ~205 F-category pairs, how many are decoder-competition vs feature-fragmentation?
Auto-discovery: can we replace the hand-curated competitor list with a procedure (e.g. all single-token cities sharing the target state region whose steered prob > 5x baseline)?
Joint probability: ' Mont' has high rank because it is shared across Montana/Montgomery/etc.; the joint ' Mont' * 'pelier' may be a fairer rank metric for multi-token capitals.
Cross-dataset replication: does the same split exist in books/products/paintings/sounds-colors?
